proposals.before: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. The Xiancheng family originally sprang from the Xi people; in his day Shi Xiancheng was reckoned a man of Jiankang in Lingwu.
proposals.after: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. His ancestors originally sprang from the Xi people; in his day Shi Xiancheng was reckoned a man of Jiankang in Lingwu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 其先 refers to Shi Xiancheng's ancestors, not a 'Xiancheng family' as if Xiancheng were the surname.

proposals.before: When he soon heard that Qi had been killed by his own officers, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian — no better than a dog — and a dog knows only its master.
proposals.after: When he soon heard that Qi had been killed by his own officers, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian—no better than a dog—and knows only his master.
proposals.reason: Source compares Xiancheng himself to a dog that knows its master; English should keep the self-reference clear without inventing a generic dog subject.

proposals.before: In the third year of Taihe the soldiers killed Shi Xiancheng and cried out together, "Let Lord He of Duan, chief controller of the headquarters guard, take charge as acting governor, and the three armies will be settled."
proposals.after: In the third year of Taihe the soldiers killed Shi Xiancheng and cried out together, "Let Lord He, the chief controller of the headquarters guard, take charge as acting governor, and the three armies will be settled."
proposals.reason: 端公 is a respectful form of address for a censorial officer, not a place-name 'Duan'.

proposals.before: In the eleventh year of his rule his own soldiers killed him.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year [of Xiantong] his own soldiers killed him.
proposals.reason: 十一年 continues the Xiantong chronology (cf. s0080 咸通十一年), not an ordinal count of Quanhao's years in office.

proposals.before: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxing Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
proposals.after: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxiang, Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
proposals.reason: 新鄕 is Xinxiang; the English fuses the place-name with Shuang into 'Xinxing Shuang'.

proposals.after: Hongxin's son Wei — Wei, styled Duanji.
proposals.reason: Heading 弘信子 威威 repeats the given name as biography lemma; keep the lemma break without dropping the courtesy name.

proposals.before: In praise it is said: In praise it is said: To seize by force and rule by righteousness — even antiquity knew such cases.
proposals.after: In praise it is said: To seize by force and rule by righteousness — even antiquity knew such cases.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English duplicates the formula 'In praise it is said:' ; the Chinese heading should yield a single formula before the maxim.

proposals.before: Praise says: Praise says: To seize by rebellion and preserve by compliance — antiquity too has known this.
proposals.after: Praise says: To seize by rebellion and preserve by compliance — antiquity too has known this.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise doubles 'Praise says:' mirroring the duplicated 贊贊 opening; keep a single praise formula.

decisions.reason: s0001 其先出於奚虜 means his ancestors came from the Xi; 憲誠 is the given name of 史憲誠, so "the Xiancheng family" wrongly treats the given name as a surname. "His ancestors" restores the Chinese sense.

s0019 憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主 compares Xiancheng himself to a dog that only recognizes its master; the original invents a second generic dog subject ("a dog knows only its master"). The proposed wording keeps Xiancheng as the subject of 識主.
s0058 何端公 is respectful address for the censorial officer He (cf. s0057 兼侍御史), not "Lord He of Duan" as if 端 were a place-name. Dropping "of Duan" matches the Chinese title.

decisions.after: In the eleventh year of Xiantong his own soldiers killed him.
decisions.reason: s0071 十一年 is a reign-year date, not "the eleventh year of his rule"; related evidence (s0080 咸通十一年) shows the Xiantong era. The proposal correctly rejects the tenure reading, but bracketed "[of Xiantong]" is awkward; write the era in plain English.
s0098 行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊 separates the place 新鄕 (Xinxiang) from 爽 (Zhuge Shuang). "Xinxing Shuang" wrongly fuses them; "near Xinxiang, Shuang's troops" restores the parse.
s0161 弘信子威…字端己 is fully covered by "Hongxin's son Wei, styled Duanji." Doubling "Wei — Wei" only mirrors a lemma typography and yields awkward English without correcting any semantic error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 弘信子 威威，字端己

decisions.reason: s0212 opens 贊贊曰 with a duplicated praise formula reflected as "In praise it is said:" twice; a single formula before 逆取順守 is the correct idiomatic rendering.
The literal field of the same unit likewise doubles "Praise says:" against 贊贊曰; keeping one praise formula before the maxim matches the intended encomium opening.
